findings.location: amendment.json ownerDecisions[6]; changes[SEC-4 PACKETS_ADDED].source, changes[HI-7 PACKETS_ADDED].source
findings.finding: The new entry reads "Owner (2026-10-16, relayed by the lane monitor, verbatim): SEC-4 for OBSERVER rests on: ...". The bullet is verbatim (OWNER_DECISIONS.md:53), but the entry does not say which decision it is. The two T04 rows cite "owner decision Q-HE4A-B2 (a)". Of all decision ids cited in change sources, Q-HE4A-B2 is the only one that appears in no ownerDecisions entry (scripted check). The HI-7 T04 row also cites Q-HE4A-B2, but that decision speaks of SEC-4 only. HI-7's T04 items come from HE-004A's carried list.
findings.requiredChange: Label the entry "Owner, Q-HE4A-B2 = (a) (2026-10-16, relayed by the lane monitor, verbatim): SEC-4 for OBSERVER rests on: ...". This follows the relayed header "Owner decision Q-HE4A-B2 = (a), 2026-10-16." and leaves out its relay instruction. Cite HI-7's T04 row to HE-004A's carried items only (R10 MODEL_DEFINED at a34a429, HE-004A 'Carried', T04).

findings.finding: dependencyNames maps "the I06 successor" to "plan v2's W02G-F2 (the I06 successor bound to the production profile)" and calls native-profile v4 "not a plan v2 packet". HE-004D2 waits for 'the I06 successor' by Q-HE4B-11 (b). DESIGN-B section 1.1 gives that decision's basis: "I06 R1-4 makes every W02a successor need an I06 successor", so the I06 successor HE-004D2 waits for is the one bound to native-profile v4. That is W02G-F2 only if native-profile v4 is, or leads directly to, the production profile W02A-F2, which neither decision states. The term is also used in a second sense in HE-004C's summary (the W02-PROD successor of the dossier's Q-HE4-6). With one fixed mapping, HE-004D2 could be sequenced after the production I06 successor without any decision saying so.
findings.requiredChange: Map it as the sources support, e.g. "the I06 successor bound to native-profile v4 (I06 R1-4); W02G-F2 when native-profile v4 is the production profile W02A-F2". Keep the W02-PROD sense separate, as "W02G-F2", in HE-004C's summary. Alternatively, get the monitor to confirm that the two are the same.

findings.finding: The note says "consumerPacket names the packet that first holds the files: the plan v2 packet for rows registered before a split (HE-004, ...) and the R10 packet where the plan already names it (HE-003A2; HE-003A3, ...)". Two parts are inaccurate. (a) Neither plan v2 nor amendment 1 names HE-003A2: plan v2 names HE-003, and HE-003A2 is an R10 part. (b) B1's 10 rows are registered in the same packet that publishes the split, not before it, and B1's files are first held by HE-004B1. By the note's own rule they would be labelled HE-004B1, yet they carry HE-004. This also clashes with notes[1], which justifies HE-004 by the bytes rule.
findings.requiredChange: Restate the convention to match the rows, e.g. "consumerPacket is a label; the edge rule binds bytes, modes and versions. Carried rows keep their labels (v3 used the R10 part HE-003A2). B1's rows use the plan v2 packet HE-004, which this packet refines (HE-004B1 first holds them). The I05 v4 rows use HE-003A3, which this packet adds." Alternatively, relabel B1's rows HE-004B1.

findings.finding: The rule says each holder "has a REFINED row", not exactly one. refined() computes 'before' from the post-amendment-1 list, not from the running state, so the builder would accept a second REFINED row for the same obligation. Applied in order, such a row has nothing to replace, so the content is sound today (one REFINED row per obligation, checked).
findings.requiredChange: Optional: write "exactly one REFINED row", and have the packet checker apply rows in order against the running list.
